candidates.attacker_control: The attacker chooses the request target of an unauthenticated GET to any path covered by a Shiro chain that requires authentication (e.g., a victim clicks/loads a URL such as https://victim-host//attacker.example/path). That raw URI is what the servlet container returns from getRequestURI() and is what SavedRequest persists; no sanitization or same-origin check is applied before it becomes the post-login Location header.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked for any same-origin/internal-path validation in the redirect path: none exists anywhere in the repository (searched for isValidInternalPath, startsWith("//"), scheme checks; no matches). Noted that WebUtils.getRequestUri()/getPathWithinApplication() deliberately decode, strip semicolons and normalize/collapse '//', but SavedRequest does not use those helpers, so the fix pattern exists in the codebase yet is absent on this sink. Verified RedirectView only prepends the context path when contextRelative==true, and WebUtils explicitly sets it false for saved requests. Verified the saved request is only honored for GET (WebUtils.java:687), so POST-based attempts fall back to the configured successUrl. Verified InvalidRequestFilter is opt-in and does not flag double slashes. Considered that many containers may normalize or reject leading '//' or backslash forms before getRequestURI() is observed; Tomcat's normalization applies to the decoded mapping URI while getRequestURI() returns the raw URI, but this depends on container/version and could not be verified statically. No runtime confirmation was performed.
candidates.impact: Post-authentication open redirect: a victim who logs in after following a crafted link is sent to an attacker-controlled origin. This enables phishing on a trusted-looking login flow, credential/session harvesting, and leakage of tokens or referrer data to the attacker's site. Severity is moderate (redirect-only, but it violates the trust boundary that the saved-request mechanism is supposed to stay inside the application).
candidates.prerequisites: 1) Shiro web application using form/basic authentication with a protected chain (the default FormAuthenticationFilter.saveRequestAndRedirectToLogin behavior must run, i.e., authc/user filter on the requested path). 2) The request must be a GET (WebUtils.java:687 only uses the saved request for GET). 3) The victim must complete a successful authentication after the crafted request is saved. 4) The servlet container must preserve the crafted prefix (leading '//', or backslash form with ALLOW_BACKSLASH-style configuration) in getRequestURI(); containers that reject or normalize such URIs at the connector level would mitigate. 5) InvalidRequestFilter must be absent or must allow the crafted form (its default checks cover ';', backslash, non-ASCII, %2e/%2f traversal patterns, but not a leading '//').
candidates.root_cause: The request-restoration flow stores the raw, undecoded request URI and later uses it as an absolute redirect target without checking that it is an internal path. SavedRequest stores request.getRequestURI() verbatim (SavedRequest.java:43-47) and getRequestUrl() concatenates it with the query string (SavedRequest.java:61-67). WebUtils.redirectToSavedRequest() takes that value for GET requests and sets contextRelative=false (WebUtils.java:682-690), then issueRedirect -> RedirectView.renderMergedOutputModel() skips context-path prepending and RedirectView.sendRedirect() passes it to HttpServletResponse.sendRedirect()/Location with no scheme, host, or same-origin check (RedirectView.java:190-204, 295-306). A URI beginning with two slashes (or a backslash variant where backslashes are permitted) is therefore emitted as a protocol-relative Location value and interpreted by browsers as an external origin.
candidates.title: Post-authentication open redirect via unvalidated SavedRequest URL in WebUtils.redirectToSavedRequest
candidates.trace: 1. Unauthenticated GET with crafted raw URI (e.g. //attacker.example/x) hits a Shiro-protected chain; PathMatchingFilterChainResolver matches an authc chain and AccessControlFilter.onAccessDenied -> saveRequestAndRedirectToLogin (AccessControlFilter.java:190-193). 2. WebUtils.saveRequest creates SavedRequest, whose constructor stores request.getRequestURI() unchanged (SavedRequest.java:46); the user is redirected to the login URL. 3. Victim submits credentials to the login URL; FormAuthenticationFilter.onAccessDenied -> executeLogin -> subject.login succeeds (AuthenticatingFilter.java:51-54). 4. FormAuthenticationFilter.onLoginSuccess -> AuthenticationFilter.issueSuccessRedirect -> WebUtils.redirectToSavedRequest (FormAuthenticationFilter.java:196-200, AuthenticationFilter.java:93-95). 5. Because the saved method is GET, successUrl = savedRequest.getRequestUrl() and contextRelative=false (WebUtils.java:687-689). 6. issueRedirect -> RedirectView.renderMergedOutputModel: contextRelative is false, so no context path is prepended; sendRedirect emits Location: //attacker.example/x (RedirectView.java:195-203, 295-305). 7. The browser resolves the protocol-relative Location against the attacker's origin, completing the open redirect after a trusted login flow.
candidates.unverified: Container-specific acceptance/preservation of '//' (or backslash variants) in getRequestURI() could not be verified statically; therefore actual exploitability is not proven. It is also unverified whether the benchmark's intended defect for this snapshot is this open redirect or the separate path-confusion class noted in rejected leads. No runtime, test, or patch comparison was performed.

coverage_summary: Reviewed the assigned snapshot of Apache Shiro 1.12.0 (759 source files; binaries/symlinks/sensitive-path exclusions all reported as zero, tests are not present). Read/search-sampled the web security surface (InvalidRequestFilter, PathMatchingFilterChainResolver/AntPathMatcher, PathMatchingFilter/AccessControlFilter, FormAuthenticationFilter/AuthenticatingFilter/HttpAuthenticationFilter, WebUtils/SavedRequest/RedirectView, PortFilter/SslFilter/LogoutFilter, CookieRememberMeManager/SimpleCookie, DefaultWebSessionManager/SimpleCookie session handling, AbstractShiroFilter, ShiroHttpServletRequest), core authentication/authorization (Simple/Hashed credentials matchers, DefaultPasswordService, WildcardPermission, AuthorizingRealm, ModularRealmAuthorizer, DefaultSecurityManager, DefaultSubjectDAO, SimplePrincipalCollection), session management, remember-me serialization, crypto cipher/hash/RNG, JdbcRealm, config/ogdl interpolation, and JNDI/LDAP entry points. Search passes covered redirect sinks, URI normalization, deserialization, JNDI lookups, SecureRandom usage, and authorization checks. This is a sampling review, not an exhaustive line-by-line reading of all 759 files.
limitations: No code execution, tests, containers, or exploit payloads were used, so all conclusions are static and none are runtime-confirmed.
Container-specific URI handling (whether a leading '//' or backslash survives in getRequestURI for the affected deployment) could not be verified.
Only 759 main-source files were visible; tests and build products that could corroborate intended behavior are absent.
No access to git history, patches, advisories, or external databases, so I could not confirm which known issue this snapshot was selected for.
The single-candidate cap means other plausible-but-unproven classes were recorded only as rejected leads.

rejected_leads.lead: Path traversal / filter-chain authentication bypass around WebUtils.getPathWithinApplication and PathMatchingFilterChainResolver (e.g. semicolon or encoded-dot/slash forms).
rejected_leads.reason: The snapshot already contains the historical defenses (removeSemicolon + normalize in getPathWithinApplication, trailing-slash handling in PathMatchingFilterChainResolver, and InvalidRequestFilter's blockTraversal/isNormalized plus %2e/%2f checks). I could not derive a concrete request form that both reaches a protected resource and resolves to a path Shiro considers unprotected, so this remains an unconfirmed lead rather than a candidate.

Deserialization is preceded by AES decryption with a per-instance randomly generated key (AbstractRememberMeManager constructor) and no hardcoded/default key is present, so attacker control of a usable serialized payload is not supported by the source.
The redirect host is derived from the Host header, which a remote victim's browser normally sets to the victim application host; no cross-site vector is evident from source.

rejected_leads.lead: JNDI/LDAP/reflection or ini-interpolation injection (JndiObjectFactory, JndiTemplate, ReflectionBuilder, CommonsInterpolator).
rejected_leads.reason: These paths consume server-side configuration values, not remote request data; not an externally reachable vulnerability in this snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: Weak crypto / credential-handling defects (AES defaults, hash iterations, credential comparison).
rejected_leads.reason: AesCipherService defaults to GCM with generated IVs, SecureRandom-based RNG, and MessageDigest.isEqual comparisons; the inspected password/hash services match the documented secure defaults.

summary: Repository is Apache Shiro 1.12.0 (759 main-source files; tests absent). The strongest source-evidenced issue is an open-redirect chain in the form/login flow: the raw request URI captured in SavedRequest is later fed, unvalidated and with contextRelative=false, into the redirect machinery. I found no hardening/validation anywhere that restricts the post-login redirect target to the current origin. Other candidate classes (path-confusion/filter-chain bypass, remember-me deserialization, Host-header redirects) could not be substantiated from source alone and are listed as rejected/unconfirmed leads.
